launchable_note: The C32 sweep ran to completion and FAILED. The lifecycle records an attested negative result; it is not launchable and must not be read as certified.
purpose: Record the certification contract lifecycle. Stage attested_fail means a registered contract was executed to completion and FAILED; the sweep attestation for it is registered at registered_sweep_attestation_path and is present. (Earlier text here said the attestation was intentionally absent -- that was C26, which was registered and never executed.)

supersedes.why: C26 pinned the 51-patch engine and the pre-C28 readout. It was registered, its launcher enforcement and contract attestation were completed, and then a pre-launch diagnostic showed it would fail with roughly 4,800 unattributed rows. The sweep was deliberately held rather than spent, so its eight 1,250-game blocks from 16,000,000 remain unconsumed. Its artifacts stay as immutable evidence and its seed blocks stay burned rather than recycled.

matcher_era_note: differential_sha256 is pinned here as well as the readout hash, because the fidelity KPI's two terms both come from the differential. A KPI reading is comparable only against another sharing this hash.
successor_registration_note: source_code_identity is a frozen, CORRECT snapshot of the classifier at the pinned certification commit -- the classifier the C32 sweep actually executed (the attestation's runtime_readout_sha256 matches it under enforcement_status enforced). The working tree has since moved past it. C32 is therefore an ATTESTED HISTORICAL result and no longer the active registration. A successor contract must be registered before another sweep runs, and C32 must never be re-scored with the current classifier. The live hashes are in successor_pending_identity, which IS asserted; do not restate them here, because prose is not tested and goes stale silently.

successor_pending_identity.why_pinned: A boolean 'we have diverged' flag is not a binding -- review passed four tampers with it set, including one that laundered every real unattributed row into a documented family. These are the EXACT bytes the divergence is declared for. Any further edit to either file breaks the assertion and forces a reviewable update here, which is the point. UPDATED 2026-08-07 (C144): both files moved. The differential gained verdict_partition_failures() -- the four-term boundary verdict identity, mechanized -- and the readout now gates on it per shard and computes in_support_rate over the ADJUDICATED denominator rather than boundaries_measured. Neither of C144's OWN edits touches classification or attribution, so they re-derive no certification number. But that is not the whole record for the new hash, and saying only that would repeat the defect C144 is about. THIS PIN WAS ALREADY STALE. It was last accurate at #1032 (5d7f2ed0, 2026-08-02) and was broken by #1054 (5475b2da, 2026-08-03), so tests/test_c26_damage_composition_readout.py::test_production_matcher_is_not_the_rejected_experiment has been RED on main since then. Seven merged PRs have touched the differential in between -- #1054, #1059, #1086, #1107, #1122, #1135, #1149 -- for a net +470/-12 lines, and FOUR of them are matcher or classifier changes whose effect on classification was never declared here: #1054 (movepainsplit inherits the damage roll, 35 -> 31), #1059 (faint-without-damage synthesis and the Air Lock speed guard, 21 -> 13), #1086 (demote the drag limit to a last resort) and #1107 (forced-replacement ply runs no residual phase). The delta from 8f83a11f to this hash absorbs all of them. Re-stamping this pin is therefore NOT the routine no-op it looks like, and a future re-stamp should say which changes it is certifying rather than only the ones in the PR doing the stamping. See reports/c144_boundary_identity_correction.md. UPDATED 2026-08-07 (C142): both files moved again. Taking C144's instruction that a re-stamp must say which changes it certifies rather than only that it happened, and declaring the classification effect explicitly rather than asserting there is none. The differential gained a FIFTH boundary verdict, skip:rump_branch_set -- a boundary whose branch set was left incomplete before comparison has its verdict WITHHELD instead of adjudicated -- plus withheld_repros retention, strict:lossy_render_marker:* attribution, strict:diverged_on_full_branch_set, and VERDICT_PARTITION_SKIP_COUNTERS carrying the new verdict into C144's mechanized partition. The readout's change is that unadjudicated now sums every post-measurement skip verdict rather than only the lossy one, so in_support_rate is computed over a denominator that excludes withheld boundaries. THIS RE-STAMP DOES TOUCH CLASSIFICATION, unlike C144's: a boundary that previously reported transition:diverged on a rump branch set now reports no verdict at all. Its MEASURED effect on the two open windows is ZERO -- skip:rump_branch_set is 0 on both dev 19,000,000-199 and holdout 19,100,000-199, matched and diverged are unchanged against a baseline taken at the merge base on the same engine fingerprint 5fa147ffa325c887, and the only counter deltas are the new counters appearing. So it re-derives no certification number on any window this program has swept, but it WOULD change one on a window carrying a rump boundary -- C141's final holdout is such a window, at 1 divergence and 1 withheld rather than 2 divergences. That is the honest statement rather than no classification effect. See reports/c142_rump_branch_adjudication.md.

pinned_source_commit_reachability: C32's required_source_commit is NOT an ancestor of main -- it lives on scott/engine-fidelity-program, the branch the split PRs came from. Three registration tests resolve it with `git show` and hard-ERROR in a default single-branch clone (what actions/checkout does). They now SKIP instead, which is honest: in a shallow clone the provenance genuinely cannot be verified. DO NOT DELETE scott/engine-fidelity-program until this contract is superseded, or the object becomes unreachable on origin and C32's whole provenance chain is permanently unverifiable.
